children: Lockheed Martin will pay $29.5 million to resolve federal allegations that it discriminated against white workers as part of its diversity, equity and inclusion policies.

It is the latest settlement stemming from investigations launched by the Trump administration in a broad effort to root out diversity initiatives at major U.S. companies contracting with the federal government. Companies including Deloitte, Accenture and IBM have reached similar settlements with the Justice Department.

Lockheed Martin denied any wrongdoing and said the allegations related to programs it already ended. It agreed to settle the matter "to avoid the distraction and expense of prolonged litigation," the defense contractor said.

The Justice Department alleged the company failed to comply with antidiscrimination requirements in its federal contracts. It claimed Lockheed Martin gave preference to employees from minority groups when making pay, promotion and hiring decisions. Specifically it claimed its human-resources staff pressured leaders to remove nonminority employees from lists of those eligible for incentive payments to make room for those from minority groups.

The Trump administration has been investigating companies that contract with the federal government under a novel use of the False Claims Act. The law, typically used to police Medicare or Medicaid fraud, is designed to penalize businesses that defraud the government by inflating the cost of services. In the second Trump administration, the Justice Department has operated under the theory that considering race or gender in employment practices is, in effect, fraud against the government.
Under the whistleblower provision of the Act, Tim Booher, a former vice president at Lockheed, will receive $4.4 million from the settlement, the department said.

The settlement also resolves a 2025 charge filed by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, under which Lockheed will pay $7.5 million to 1,000 Lockheed employees. According to the government, that is the largest class of workers to publicly recover money through an EEOC settlement stemming from corporate DEI practices.
